Q: Nx publish is releasing all the packages in independent mode with wrong tags A:

Check that there are no changes that nx picks up:

git log --stat package@1.2.0..HEAD -- package.json packages/package-a

If there are changes to the project-level package.json in dependencies/devDependencies, nx will bump your project version instead of logging this message:

package-a 🚫 No changes were detected using git history and the conventional commits standard

Q: ModelCheckpoint not saveing last validating checkpoint when save_last=True A:

To save both the best validated and last validated

You need two separate ModelCheckpoint callbacks.

best_checkpoint = ModelCheckpoint(
    dirpath="path/to/dir",
    monitor="val_loss",
    mode="min",
    filename="best_model",
    save_top_k=1,
)

and

last_checkpoint = ModelCheckpoint(
    dirpath="path/to/dir",
    filename="last_model",
    save_top_k=0,          #
    save_last=True,        # always keep last.ckpt
    every_n_epochs=1       
)

now use both the checkpoints in trainer

trainer = Trainer(
    callbacks=[best_checkpoint, last_checkpoint],
    max_epochs=20,
    accelerator="gpu",
    val_check_interval=0.2,
    log_every_n_steps=1,
)

The last checkpoint can also be saved manually after completing the training

trainer.save_checkpoint("path/to/dir/final_epoch.ckpt")

Q: GET request to an API endpoint comes back as 403 forbidden even with headers using httr package in R. (works in browser) A:

Using the headers obtained via browser tools works just fine.

library(httr)

url = "https://www.sofascore.com/api/v1/sport/esports/scheduled-events/2025-03-13"

headers <- add_headers(
  "accept"= "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/avif,image/webp,image/apng,*/*;q=0.8,application/signed-exchange;v=b3;q=0.7",
  "accept-language"= "en,de-DE;q=0.9,de;q=0.8,en-US;q=0.7,zh-CN;q=0.6,zh;q=0.5",
  "cache-control"= "no-cache",
  "pragma"= "no-cache",
  "priority"= "u=0, i",
  "sec-ch-ua"= "\"Not(A:Brand\";v=\"8\", \"Chromium\";v=\"144\", \"Google Chrome\";v=\"144\"",
  "sec-ch-ua-mobile"= "?0",
  "sec-ch-ua-platform"= "\"Windows\"",
  "sec-fetch-dest"= "document",
  "sec-fetch-mode"= "navigate",
  "sec-fetch-site"= "cross-site",
  "sec-fetch-user"= "?1",
  "upgrade-insecure-requests"= "1"
)

response = GET(url, headers)

response$status_code
# [1] 200
result <- content(response)

str(result, max.level = 2)
# List of 1
# $ events:List of 86
# ..$ :List of 23
# ..$ :List of 23
# ..$ :List of 23
# ..$ :List of 23

Q: Getting “Sizes of tensors must match” error when using ComfyUI WanVideoWrapper (wan2.2) to generate video A:

I’ve encountered a similar issue before.
The reason is that the DWPose node in your workflow alters the image size, even if you’ve already resized the video and reference image to 480×832. The solution is to add a Resize Image node after the DWPose node to resize the output back to 480×832.
Hope this helps!

Q: Want to hide command prompt window in using WshShell.Exec method A:

I know this thread is quite old, but I just came up against the same problem and found a solution by adding "exit" to the command string, which closes the window.

From the cmd page of Microsoft Docs:
You can specify multiple commands for [string]. Separate them by the command separator && and enclose them in quotation marks. For example:

"[command1]&&[command2]&&[command3]"

So the full command string you pass to WshShell.Exec would look like this:

        cmd.exe /c "java -classpath . HelloWorld&&exit"

Q: How to concatenate String Tensors with tensorflow.js? A:

You can convert each Tensor to an array and create a new tensor:

var c = tf.tensor2d([
  ["1.0", "2.0", "3.0"],
  ["10.0", "20.0", "30.0"]
]);
var d = tf.tensor2d([
  ["8.0", "7.0", "5.0"],
  ["3.0", "11.0", "23.0"]
]);

var c_concat_d = tf.tensor([c.arraySync(), d.arraySync()])
c_concat_d.print();
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tensorflow/tfjs@2.0.0/dist/tf.min.js"></script>

Note: This uses a more recent version of tensorflow.js than the one used by the OP.

Q: What is the use case of this TensorFlow class: image.flip_up_down? A:

tf.image provides all sorts of general-purpose image manipulation functions, letting you avoid having to deal with multi-dimensional numpy arrays directly (or even worse, using OpenCV functions). Maybe your dataset just has all images upside-down and you need to correct that.

Flipping can also be part of data augmentation, but this is easier done as a keras layer layers.RandomFlip("vertical"). Vertical flipping is less common than horizontal flipping, because in most cases you don't need to model upside-down images.

Q: how to search for links using telethon A:

get_messages (or iter_messages) supports filter argument that takes any of MessagesFilter constructors.

so in your case, use:

await client.get_messages(chat,
    filter=telethon.types.InputMessagesFilterUrl()
)
